blocks.prompt: 1. The OOP concept that hides data inside a class is:

options.text: Inheritance
Polymorphism
Encapsulation
Abstraction

blocks.explanation: Encapsulation data aur methods ko class mein band karti aur data tak seedhi pohanch rokti hai (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 2. Classes and objects in Object-Oriented Programming are best described as:

options.text: Classes are real-world entities, and objects are methods.
Classes are blueprints, and objects are instances of those blueprints.
Classes are used for data storage, and objects are used for functionality.
Objects define functionality, and classes store data.

blocks.explanation: Class blueprint (naqsha) hai; object us class ka instance hai jis mein asal values hoti hain (3.2, Figure 3.1).

blocks.prompt: 3. The main idea behind encapsulation in OOP is:

options.text: To hide data inside a class and prevent unauthorised access.
To create a flexible and adaptable programme.
To reuse code from other classes.
To allow multiple inheritance in classes.

blocks.explanation: Encapsulation data ko class ke andar rakh kar be-ijazat pohanch se bachati hai; lachak polymorphism aur dobara istemal inheritance ka kaam hai (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 4. Inheritance in OOP means:

options.text: Reusing and extending functionality from a parent class to a child class.
Hiding data in a class.
Creating multiple instances of the same class.
Managing polymorphic behaviour of classes.

blocks.explanation: Inheritance mein child class parent se properties aur methods leti aur un mein izafa ya tabdeeli karti hai: reuse aur extend (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 5. Polymorphism in OOP is best defined as:

options.text: Allowing an object to take multiple forms through method overriding.
Hiding data inside a class for security.
Using multiple inheritance to extend classes.
Ensuring that each object has only one method.

blocks.explanation: Polymorphism ka matlab "kai shaklein": aik hi method mukhtalif objects ke liye alag kaam karta hai, maslan Dog aur Cat mein override kiya gaya sound() (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 6. An example of inheritance in Python is:

options.text: Creating two classes with similar attributes.
A child class inheriting attributes and methods from a parent class.
Using private variables within a class.
Modifying a method inside the same class.

blocks.explanation: class Dog(Animal) mein child class Dog parent Animal ke attributes aur methods le leti hai (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 7. The purpose of polymorphism in programming is:

options.text: To create reusable functions with multiple parameter types.
To allow a function or method to have different implementations.
To combine different classes into a single class.
To manage the flow of control in a programme.

blocks.explanation: Polymorphism aik hi method naam ko mukhtalif implementations deta hai, maslan har payment type ka apna processPayment() (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 8. The keyword used to define a class in Python is:

options.text: def
class
function
object

blocks.explanation: Class keyword class se banti hai, maslan class Student: ; def function ya method banata hai (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 9. Encapsulation is best described as:

options.text: Combining data and methods into a single unit and controlling access to data.
Combining multiple classes into one class.
Inheriting methods from other classes.
Allowing objects to have multiple forms.

blocks.explanation: Encapsulation data (variables) aur methods (functions) ko aik unit (class) mein jorti aur data tak seedhi pohanch control karti hai (3.2).

blocks.prompt: 10. Inheritance allows a class to:

options.text: Hide its data only.
Inherit attributes and methods from another class.
Define multiple functions only.
Create objects without a class.

blocks.explanation: Inheritance aik class ko doosri class ki properties aur methods lene deti hai (3.2, Summary).

blocks.prompt:
1. What is Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)?
(OOP kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: OOP classes aur objects se program banane ka tareeqa hai, jis mein har object asal duniya ki cheez (properties aur behaviour ke saath) hota hai. Is mein encapsulation, inheritance aur polymorphism hain, jo modularity, reusability aur aasan maintenance dete hain.

blocks.prompt:
2. What is the purpose of a class in Python?
(Python mein class ka maqsad kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Class blueprint (naqsha) hai jo kisi cheez ke attributes (data) aur methods (kaam) tay karti hai. Is se milte julte kai objects banaye jate hain aur data aur us ke functions aik jagah rehte hain.

blocks.prompt:
3. What is the difference between a class and an object?
(Class aur object mein kya farq hai?)
blocks.explanation: Class naqsha (blueprint) hai; object us naqshe se bani asal cheez (instance) hai.

rows: Blueprint ya template (naqsha)
Class ka instance (asal cheez)
Attributes aur methods tay karti hai
Attributes ki asal values rakhta hai
Keyword class se aik dafa banti hai
Aik class se kai objects ban sakte hain
Misal: class Student
Misal: object1 = Student("Ali")

blocks.prompt:
4. What is purpose of __init__...?
(__init__ ka maqsad kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: __init__ class ka constructor method hai. Object bante hi yeh khud chalta hai aur object ke attributes ki shuru ki values set karta hai, maslan Student("Ali") mein self.name = name.

blocks.prompt:
5. What is encapsulation in OOP, and why is it important?
(Encapsulation kya hai aur kyun zaroori hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Encapsulation data (variables) aur methods ko aik unit (class) mein band karti aur data tak seedhi pohanch rokti hai.
Ahmiyat: data ko ghair zaroori pohanch se bachati, security barhati, code sambhalna aasan aur tabdeeli sirf control ke saath.

blocks.prompt:
6. How does encapsulation help in keeping data secure and private?
(Encapsulation data ko mehfooz aur private kaise rakhti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Data private bana diya jata hai (self.__balance) taake bahar se seedha na badla ja sake; Python ki name mangling ittefaqi pohanch rokti hai. Data sirf methods jaise deposit(), withdraw() aur get_balance() se parha ya badla jata hai, jo pehle values check kar sakte hain.

blocks.prompt:
7. What is inheritance in OOP, and how does it help in reusing functionality?
(Inheritance kya hai aur functionality reuse karne mein kaise madad deti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Inheritance child class ko parent class ki properties aur methods lene deti hai. Parent ka code aik dafa likha jata aur har child class use istemal karti hai, is se dohrao (redundancy) kam hota hai; maslan Dog(Animal) Animal ka eat() baghair dobara likhe istemal karti hai.

blocks.prompt:
8. How does inheritance enable the extension of functionality in Python?
(Inheritance functionality barhane (extension) mein kaise madad karti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Child class parent ki har cheez rakhti hai aur naye methods jor sakti ya purane override kar sakti hai, is liye purana code dobara likhe baghair program barhta hai. Misal: Dog(Animal) bark() jorti hai; super() se parent ka method bhi bulaya ja sakta hai.

blocks.prompt:
9. What is polymorphism in OOP, and how does it make code more flexible?
(Polymorphism kya hai aur code ko lachakdar kaise banata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Polymorphism ka matlab "kai shaklein": aik hi method, function ya operator object ke mutabiq alag kaam karta hai. Code mukhtalif objects par aik hi method (maslan sound()) bulata hai aur har object apne tareeqe se jawab deta hai, is liye nayi classes calling code badle baghair fit ho jati hain.

blocks.prompt:
10. How does polymorphism help in creating adaptable and reusable code?
(Polymorphism adaptable aur reusable code banane mein kaise madad karta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Aik common interface (method ka naam) aik dafa likha aur kai qism ke objects ke liye dobara istemal hota hai; har class apni implementation deti hai. Misal: processPayment() Credit Card, UPI, NetBanking aur Wallet sab ke liye; naye payment type ko sirf apna processPayment() chahiye.

blocks.prompt:
1. Explain the concept of classes and objects in Object-Oriented Programming (OOP).
(OOP mein classes aur objects ka concept samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Class: blueprint ya template jo kisi cheez ki properties (attributes) aur kaam (methods) tay karti hai. Keyword class se banti hai.
Object: class ka instance jo attributes ki asal values rakhta hai aur asal duniya ki cheez ko dikhata hai.

Aham nukaat:
- Classes aur objects asal duniya ki cheezon ko code mein dikhate hain (maslan class Person: attributes name, age, gender aur methods eat(), sleep(), work(); objects P1 = Bob, P2 = Jenny).
- Aik class se kai objects bante hain; har object ka apna data.
- __init__ constructor hai jo object bante waqt values set karta hai; self maujooda object hai.
- Data aur us ke functions aik jagah, is liye program tarteeb wala, modular aur reusable.

Misal program:
class Student:
    def __init__(self, name, marks):
        self.name = name
        self.marks = marks

    def display(self):
        print("Name:", self.name, "| Marks:", self.marks)

s1 = Student("Ali", 85)
s2 = Student("Sara", 92)
s1.display()
s2.display()

Output:
Name: Ali | Marks: 85
Name: Sara | Marks: 92

Yahan Student class hai; s1 aur s2 do objects hain jin ka apna name aur marks hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Class ko ghar ka naqsha samjhein aur objects ko us naqshe se bane asal ghar. Naqsha aik hai, ghar kai ban sakte hain, aur har ghar ka rang (data) alag ho sakta hai.

blocks.prompt:
2. What is encapsulation in OOP?
(OOP mein encapsulation kya hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Encapsulation data (variables) aur methods (functions) ko aik unit, yani class, mein band karti aur data tak seedhi pohanch rokti hai. Data chhupa hota hai aur pohanch methods ke zariye control hoti hai.

Kyun zaroori:
- Data ko ghair zaroori pohanch se bachati hai.
- Security barhati hai.
- Code sambhalna aasan.
- Tabdeeli sirf control ke saath.

Python mein access ke levels (naming conventions, kyunke Python mein private/protected keywords nahi):
1. Public: self.name, har jagah se (default).
2. Protected: self._name (aik underscore), class aur subclasses ke liye (sirf convention).
3. Private: self.__name (do underscores), name mangling se chhupa, bahar se aasani se nahi milta.

Misal (bank account): balance chhupa hai; sirf deposit() aur withdraw() se badalta hai.
class BankAccount:
    def __init__(self, balance):
        self.__balance = balance      # private

    def deposit(self, amount):
        if amount > 0:
            self.__balance += amount

    def withdraw(self, amount):
        if amount <= self.__balance:
            self.__balance -= amount
        else:
            print("Insufficient balance")

    def get_balance(self):
        return self.__balance

account = BankAccount(1000)
account.deposit(500)
account.withdraw(300)
account.withdraw(5000)
print(account.get_balance())

Output:
Insufficient balance
1200

Seedha print(account.__balance) likhne par AttributeError aata hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Hisaab: 1000 + 500 = 1500; 1500 - 300 = 1200; 5000 nikalne ki koshish balance se zyada hai, is liye "Insufficient balance" aaya aur balance 1200 hi raha.

blocks.prompt:
3. How does inheritance work in OOP?
(OOP mein inheritance kaise kaam karti hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Inheritance aik class (child/subclass/derived) ko doosri class (parent/superclass/base) ki properties aur methods lene deti hai. Child aise banti hai: class Child(Parent):. Child parent ke members istemal kar sakti, apne jor sakti, ya unhein override kar sakti hai; super() parent ka version bulata hai.

Inheritance ki iqsam:
1. Single: aik child, sirf aik parent (Dog, Animal se).
2. Multiple: aik child, aik se zyada parents (class Child(Father, Mother); Smartphone, Camera aur Computer dono se).
3. Multilevel: zanjeer Grandparent, Parent, Child (Vehicle, Car, ElectricCar); grandchild ko dono ke members milte hain.

Misal (single inheritance aur overriding):
class Animal:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

    def eat(self):
        print(f"{self.name} is eating.")

    def sound(self):
        print("Some generic sound")

class Dog(Animal):
    def bark(self):
        print(f"{self.name} says Woof!")

    def sound(self):
        super().sound()
        print("Bark")

d = Dog("Buddy")
d.eat()
d.bark()
d.sound()

Output:
Buddy is eating.
Buddy says Woof!
Some generic sound
Bark

Dog ne eat() khud nahi likha; yeh Animal se mila. bark() Dog ne joda, aur sound() override kiya magar super().sound() ne parent ka version bhi chalaya.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Inheritance ko khandaan ki tarah samjhein: bacha walid ki aadatein (methods) virasat mein leta hai, apni nayi aadat (bark) bhi rakhta hai, aur kisi aadat ko apne andaaz mein (override) bhi kar sakta hai.

blocks.prompt:
4. What are the advantages of using inheritance in Python?
(Python mein inheritance ke fawaid kya hain?)
blocks.explanation:
Inheritance child class ko parent class reuse aur extend karne deti hai. Fawaid:
1. Code reuse: aam code parent mein aik dafa, sab children istemal karte hain.
2. Kam dohrao (redundancy).
3. Aasan izafa: naye features child class mein, purana code dobara likhe baghair.
4. Method overriding: child parent ka method apne tareeqe se likh sakti aur super() se parent ka bhi bula sakti hai.
5. Behtar tarteeb: classes ki saaf hierarchy (Vehicle, Car, ElectricCar) jo asal zindagi jaisi hai.
6. Aasan maintenance: parent mein aik islah sab children tak pohanchti hai.
7. Rawayye jorna: multiple inheritance kai parents ke features jorti hai (Smartphone = Camera + Computer).
8. Polymorphism ki bunyad: children aik hi method ko alag andaaz mein override karte hain.

Misal: Dog(Animal) eat() reuse karti aur bark() jorti hai; ElectricCar start_engine() aur drive() reuse karti aur charge() jorti hai.

blocks.prompt:
5. What is polymorphism in OOP, and how does it enhance flexibility in code?
(Polymorphism kya hai aur code mein lachak kaise barhata hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Polymorphism ka matlab "kai shaklein": aik hi method, function ya operator object ke mutabiq alag kaam karta hai.

Iqsam:
1. Compile-time polymorphism (overloading): method compile ke waqt chuna jata hai (Java, C++). Python mein asal overloading nahi; default arguments, *args/**kwargs ya conditions se aisa rawayya milta hai (maslan multiply() 0, 1, 2 ya 3 arguments ke saath).
2. Runtime polymorphism (overriding): child class parent ke method ka apna version deti hai, aur program chalte waqt object ki class dekh kar sahi version chalta hai.

Lachak kaise:
- Aik interface (method ka naam) kai qism ke objects ke liye; calling code nahi badalta.
- Nayi classes apne version ke saath jor sakte hain.
- Code reusable, adaptable aur barhane mein aasan (maslan processPayment() Credit Card, UPI, NetBanking, Wallet sab ke liye).

Misal (overriding):
class Shape:
    def area(self):
        return 0

class Rectangle(Shape):
    def __init__(self, w, h):
        self.w = w
        self.h = h

    def area(self):
        return self.w * self.h

class Circle(Shape):
    def __init__(self, r):
        self.r = r

    def area(self):
        return 3.14 * self.r * self.r

for s in [Rectangle(4, 5), Circle(2)]:
    print(type(s).__name__, s.area())
print(len("Python"), len([1, 2, 3]))
print(2 + 3, "2" + "3")

Output:
Rectangle 20
Circle 12.56
6 3
5 23

Aik hi loop har shape par area() bulata hai aur har shape apna jawab deti hai. Operators bhi polymorphic hain: + numbers jorta (5) magar strings milata ("23") hai, aur len() string aur list dono par chalta hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Hisaab: Rectangle 4 x 5 = 20; Circle 3.14 x 2 x 2 = 12.56. Method ka naam (area) aik hai, kaam shape ke mutabiq badal gaya: yahi polymorphism hai.

blocks.prompt:
6. How can encapsulation help improve data security in OOP?
(Encapsulation OOP mein data ki security kaise behtar karti hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Encapsulation data ko class ke andar chhupa kar aur sirf control wale methods se pohanch de kar security barhati hai.

Kaise:
1. Data hiding: hassas (sensitive) data private (self.__marks); bahar se seedha parha ya badla nahi ja sakta.
2. Name mangling: Python private variable ka andar ka naam badal deta hai, ittefaqi pohanch ruk jati hai.
3. Control wali pohanch: getter aur setter methods (get_marks(), set_marks()) hi rasta hain.
4. Validation: methods tabdeeli se pehle value check karte hain; ghalat value radd.
5. Access levels: public (name), protected (_name, convention) aur private (__name).
6. Mehfooz tabdeeli: class ka andar badle to bahar ka code mutasir nahi hota.

Misal:
class Student:
    def __init__(self, name, marks):
        self.name = name          # public
        self._grade = "A"         # protected (convention)
        self.__marks = marks      # private (name mangling)

    def get_marks(self):
        return self.__marks

    def set_marks(self, m):
        if 0 <= m <= 100:
            self.__marks = m
        else:
            print("Invalid marks")

s = Student("Ali", 80)
print(s.name, s._grade, s.get_marks())
s.set_marks(150)
s.set_marks(90)
print(s.get_marks())
try:
    print(s.__marks)
except AttributeError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

Output:
Ali A 80
Invalid marks
90
Error: 'Student' object has no attribute '__marks'

Ghalat marks 150 set_marks() ne radd kar diye, aur __marks tak seedhi pohanch fail hui, is liye data mehfooz raha.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Name mangling: Python andar se __marks ka naam _Student__marks kar deta hai. Is liye s.__marks likhne par woh naam nahi milta aur error aata hai. Yeh taala (lock) mukammal nahi, magar ghalti se data badalne se bachata hai.

blocks.prompt:
7. How does the combination of inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism contribute to better software design?
(Inheritance, encapsulation aur polymorphism mil kar behtar software design mein kaise madad dete hain?)
blocks.explanation:
Teeno core concepts mil kar program ko tarteeb wala, reusable, mehfooz aur sambhalne mein aasan banate hain.

1. Encapsulation: har class ka data mehfooz aur private, sirf control wale methods bahar; classes alag modules ban jati hain.
2. Inheritance: aam code parent class mein; child classes use reuse aur extend karti hain; dohrao kam.
3. Polymorphism: child classes aik hi method override karti hain; aik interface sab ke liye; naye types aasani se.

Software design ke fawaid:
- Modularity: program classes mein bata hua, har hissa alag banta aur sambhalta hai.
- Reusability: code aik dafa, istemal baar baar.
- Aasan maintenance: aik hisse ki tabdeeli poore system par asar nahi karti.
- Security: data be-ijazat pohanch se mehfooz.
- Lachak aur scalability: naye features purana code badle baghair.
- Behtar team work: saaf, samajh mein aane wala code jo asal zindagi jaisa hai.

Misal:
class Employee:
    def __init__(self, name, salary):
        self.name = name
        self.__salary = salary              # encapsulation

    def get_salary(self):
        return self.__salary

    def role(self):                        # to be overridden
        return "Employee"

class Manager(Employee):                   # inheritance
    def role(self):                        # polymorphism (overriding)
        return "Manager"

class Teacher(Employee):
    def role(self):
        return "Teacher"

for e in [Manager("Ayesha", 90000), Teacher("Bilal", 60000)]:
    print(e.name, e.role(), e.get_salary())

Output:
Ayesha Manager 90000
Bilal Teacher 60000

__salary encapsulated hai, Manager aur Teacher Employee se inherit karti hain, aur role() polymorphic hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Aik program mein teeno: salary private hai (encapsulation), Manager aur Teacher ne Employee ka code dobara nahi likha (inheritance), aur har aik ka role() alag jawab deta hai (polymorphism).

blocks.explanation: Class blueprint hai jo attributes aur methods tay karti hai; object us class ka instance hai jis mein asal values hain. Misal: class Student class hai; object1 = Student("Ali") aur object2 = Student("Ahmed") us ke do objects hain, har aik ka apna name.

rows: Blueprint ya template (naqsha)
Class ka instance (asal cheez)
Mantiqi design; batata hai object mein kya hoga
Asal cheez jis ka apna data aur rawayya
Attributes aur methods tay karti hai
Attributes ki asal values rakhta aur methods chalata hai
Keyword class se aik dafa banti hai
Class ko call kar ke banta hai: s = Student("Ali")
